stem: A company runs a TCP application on Amazon EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer in us-east-1. A standby copy runs behind a second Network Load Balancer in a second Region, us-west-2. An AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator has one listener with an endpoint group for the us-east-1 load balancer. During normal operation, all traffic must go to us-east-1. If the us-east-1 endpoints become unhealthy, traffic must move to us-west-2 automatically. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)
keywords: all traffic must go to us-east-1

options.text: Register the us-west-2 Network Load Balancer as a second endpoint in the us-east-1 endpoint group, and set the weight of that endpoint to 0.
options.why: You associate [each endpoint group with one AWS Region](../facts/global-accelerator.md#global-accelerator-listener-endpoint-group-per-region), so the us-east-1 group cannot hold a load balancer from us-west-2.
options.misconception: one endpoint group can hold endpoints from more than one Region

options.text: Add an endpoint group for us-west-2 to the existing listener, and register the us-west-2 Network Load Balancer in that endpoint group as an endpoint.
options.why: You [associate each listener with one or more endpoint](../facts/global-accelerator.md#global-accelerator-listener-endpoint-group-per-region) groups and [each endpoint group with one AWS Region](../facts/global-accelerator.md#global-accelerator-listener-endpoint-group-per-region), so us-west-2 needs its own group.

options.text: Create a second accelerator for the us-west-2 load balancer, and create Amazon Route 53 failover records with health checks that point to the two accelerators.
options.why: It works, but it adds an accelerator and DNS records, while one accelerator does not depend on [the IP address caching settings of client devices](../facts/global-accelerator.md#global-accelerator-faq-no-dns-cache-dependency-seconds).

options.text: Set the traffic dial of the us-west-2 endpoint group to 0 percent, and keep the traffic dial of the us-east-1 endpoint group at 100 percent.
options.why: A dial at 0 keeps us-west-2 out of normal traffic, and in a failover [Global Accelerator ignores the traffic dial setting](../facts/global-accelerator.md#global-accelerator-failover-to-another-endpoint-group-ignores-dial).

options.text: Set the client affinity of the listener to Source IP, so that each client keeps using the us-east-1 endpoints while those endpoints stay healthy.
options.why: Client affinity can [direct all requests from a user](../facts/global-accelerator.md#global-accelerator-client-affinity-for-stateful-apps) to the same endpoint for stateful applications; it does not choose an active Region.
options.misconception: client affinity decides which Region is active

explanation: The traffic dial supports [active-active and active-standby setups](../facts/global-accelerator.md#global-accelerator-dec-traffic-dial-weights-active-active-standby). The standby group's dial is 0, so it gets no normal traffic; when us-east-1 has no healthy endpoint, [Global Accelerator ignores the traffic dial setting](../facts/global-accelerator.md#global-accelerator-failover-to-another-endpoint-group-ignores-dial) and fails over.
takeaway: Active-standby in Global Accelerator: the standby endpoint group gets a traffic dial of 0, and failover ignores the dial.
twin: If the stem said "each Region must serve the users closest to it" instead: keep both traffic dials at their default of [100%](../facts/global-accelerator.md#global-accelerator-faq-traffic-dial-default-100-percent) after you add the second endpoint group.
say: I add a us-west-2 endpoint group with its dial at zero; failover ignores the dial, so it is a standby.
